I'll take a look, see if the same problem shows up with a simpler query/order by.
I'm confident that the problem here is not the order clause, but that the placeholders in the subqueries / union queries are not being bound correctly
I think i prefer the "tuple". Another solution could be having methods line orderAsc() and orderDesc()

Right now `->order()` can take a list of hashes like:

``` php
->order(['foo' => 'ASC', 'quux' => 'DESC'])
```

... to sort by multiple columns. Won't mixing that parameter style with the suggested tuple style create problems?

Would:

``` php
->order([$expression, 'ASC'], ['foo' => 'DESC', 'bar' => 'ASC']);
```

... then be the new interface thus order either taking either string or 1-n tuples andor hashes?

If that's not an option because `->order()` can be chained `->orderAsc()` and `->orderDesc()` easier to implement and will offer an easy interface (though you can't easily switch `ASC`/`DESC` by a string)?
Now that you bring up the multiple argument issue @ionas I would rather have `orderAsc()` and `orderDesc()` be separate methods as @lorenzo suggested.

issue.body:
The current order() method has a limitation which makes it impossible to use expression objects that also have direction. These new methods makeit easier to support directed expression objects.

I've introduced a new expression object as I felt keeping OrderByExpression simple was worth the extra bit of cost. Additionally this makes SQL injection in the ORM internals more difficult as we rely on the callers to provide a safe expression. I also experimented with an array format, but felt it left us vulnerable to the issues we've had in the past around request data manipulation.

Refs #7163
